title: Misogynoir Transformed: Black Women’s Digital Resistance

candidates.before: I was on the road to becoming a medical doctor when two things happened that made me shift course: I fell in love with women’s studies, and I got international attention as one of the leaders of a small pushback on campus against the rapper Nelly.
candidates.sentence: Both events profoundly shaped my thinking about the way Black women are treated in society and moved me to coin the term “misogynoir,” which in turn led to this book.

candidates.before: Misogynoir is not simply the racism that Black women encounter, nor is it the misogyny Black women negotiate.
candidates.sentence: Misogynoir describes the uniquely co-constitutive racialized and sexist violence that befalls Black women as a result of their simultaneous and interlocking oppression at the intersection of racial and gender marginalization.

candidates.before: Black women are caught at a vexing crossroads: hypervisible in media through misogynoir and invisible when in need of lifesaving attention.
candidates.sentence: Misogynoir is the visual representation of anti-Black misogyny not only through caricature and false representations of Black women that inform how Black women are treated, but also through the omission of Black women and girls from view altogether.
candidates.after: The so-called “missing white woman syndrome,” in which news media cover stories about missing white women and girls with a ferocity that is unmatched when women and girls of color go missing, continues to belie societal claims of growing racial equality.

candidates.before: Black feminists’ activist and scholarly interest in representation was born of these real concerns for the ways that misogynoir shapes Black women’s daily treatment in the world.
candidates.sentence: Like feminist legal scholar Kimberlé Crenshaw’s term “intersectionality,” “misogynoir” names a concept that Black feminists have discussed since our earliest preserved writings, speeches, and poetry.
candidates.after: In 1851, abolitionist Sojourner Truth revealed the ways womanhood is raced such that Black women are excluded from the category and therefore subject to abuses that white women are not.

candidates.before: Additionally, the term “Black women” is not inclusive of nonbinary, agender, and gender- variant Black folks whose experiences of misogynoir are intimately connected with a misgendering of them.
candidates.sentence: I struggled to reconcile my use of a term that is central to my definition of misogynoir yet excludes some of the people most invested in its transformation.
candidates.after: For those of us on the margins of Black womanhood, “woman” is not what we name ourselves even as misogynoir colors our experiences of the world.

candidates.before: Chapter 1 does take on this necessary project but also highlights examples that extend the possibility of misogynoir’s transformation.
candidates.sentence: The idea of misogynoir being transformed, using that swirling mass of negative energy against itself to make something altogether different, inspires me.
